title: Causal Discovery on Non-Euclidean Data

problem.claim: Causal discovery on non-Euclidean data is underexplored.

gap.claim: Existing limitations in model representations and learning algorithms have constrained causal discovery on non-Euclidean data.

contributions.claim: The Non-Euclidean Causal Model describes causal generative relationships for non-Euclidean data and introduces a tensor data type with a mapping process for the non-Euclidean causal mechanism.
The non-Euclidean Hybrid Learning method is a causal discovery algorithm based on ball covariance.
The paper generates Functional Data and Symmetric Positive Definite manifold datasets consistent with the proposed causal model.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper presents itself as the first attempt to perform causal discovery on non-Euclidean data.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on generated data and real-world data demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed NEHL method.

narrative_sequence.summary: Deep learning models for non-Euclidean data have recently begun to emerge.
Causal discovery on non-Euclidean data remains underexplored because of framework limitations.
The paper describes itself as the first attempt in this area.
The paper proposes NECM, NEHL, and two types of non-Euclidean datasets.
Experiments on generated and real-world data are reported to demonstrate NEHL effectiveness.

source_observation.claim: The paper combines a generative model, a causal discovery algorithm, and datasets designed to conform to the model.

interpretation.claim: Aligning the data representation, causal mechanism, learning method, and evaluation data can support a coherent approach to a new problem setting.

application.claim: For new structured data domains, consider designing the representation, learning procedure, and evaluation resources together.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this integrated design generalizes beyond the reported generated and real-world data.

unknowns: No quantitative experimental results or baselines are provided.
The real-world datasets and experimental settings are not described.
The abstract does not specify the limitations or scope of NECM and NEHL.
